verdict: Frozen trusted_io v1 is not launch-admissible. The 17 tests reproduce, but one protocol blocker, one resource-bound defect, and several integration/identity conditions remain.

reviewed_artifacts.hash_check: The three frozen implementation hashes matched the parent-supplied values at intake and immediately before writing this review.

findings.title: Eligible prior development candidates cannot be selected atomically
findings.requirement: The final_refit intent may name any eligible prior dev receipt/code; selection must precede final fit and must not require model-driven multi-write restoration.
findings.evidence: admit_intent persists only {state,run_id} under a closure hash (trusted_io.py:314-331,763-770). select_final_method reopens the active three-file source and requires its closure to equal the supplied historical snapshot (376-380); only then does it create final-solution.py (388-401). The synthetic final-intent change returned SNAPSHOT_CHANGED and no candidate bytes existed in private state.
findings.impact: Changing intent.json to final_refit changes the closure, and later candidates also replace active code. A valid earlier best candidate becomes unselectable. This violates the approved controller choice and can change the scientific outcome.
findings.required_fix: At development admission, atomically persist the exact opened solution.py/research.md/intent.json bytes in a private immutable store keyed by canonical closure. At selection, verify the real eligible receipt against that stored closure and copy its stored solution bytes within the same transaction. Do not restore the mutable source with multiple writes and do not create another run registry.

findings.title: max_closure_bytes is enforced after aggregate allocation
findings.requirement: File and closure caps must reject before allocating bytes beyond the relevant cap and remain bounded during reads.
findings.evidence: _snapshot_from_fd reads all three files into a tuple (524-528) and only then sums their lengths (529-530). A fixture with three 8-byte files, max_file_bytes=10, and max_closure_bytes=15 read 24 bytes in three os.read calls before LIMIT_EXCEEDED. By contrast, an 11-byte single file under max_file_bytes=10 caused zero os.read calls.
findings.impact: The configured closure memory ceiling is not the actual ceiling. Up to three per-file payloads plus chunk/join copies can be allocated before rejection.
findings.required_fix: Track a remaining closure budget and pass min(max_file_bytes, remaining_budget) into each descriptor read, so fstat rejects the next file before its content is read. Preserve the per-file cap and account for unavoidable copy overhead in the frozen numeric limit.

findings.title: Real dev-receipt provenance is an unenforced trusted-root precondition
findings.requirement: Final selection must be authorized by a real root-verified eligible development receipt, not values repeated by the controller.
findings.evidence: _permitted_receipt_tuples validates only dataclass type and lowercase SHA-256 shapes (572-581). select_final_method accepts tuple membership (382-387) but opens no receipt. A fabricated receipt hash/closure/code tuple selected successfully in the negative fixture. The method did re-open the source and selected the actual opened code hash.
findings.impact: This is safe only if the outer root bridge constructs DevResultReceipt from independently opened/verified receipt bytes and never from model arguments or the same local record being checked. The 17 tests fabricate receipts and therefore do not prove this integration fact.
findings.required_fix: Keep receipt verification in the trusted root as designed, but require launch evidence that the bridge opens the actual dev receipt at the expected trusted root, derives its receipt/closure/code fields, checks eligibility, and passes the resulting internal object. Do not expose DevResultReceipt construction to controller JSON.

findings.title: Final-refit execution identity omits fields required by the addendum
findings.requirement: The final-refit key derives trusted phase, selection receipt, selected code, task, environment, and execution configuration.
findings.evidence: _final_execution_identity includes phase, selection receipt, execution config, outer-training manifest, and hidden-features manifest (238-247), but not stored selected code, task, environment, or protocol. Two states with different selected code/task/environment produced the same execution_identity_sha256 when the same receipt token/config/manifests were supplied.
findings.impact: A correctly unique, root-verified receipt may make collision unlikely, but the identity does not satisfy the explicit protocol key and relies on an unstated transitive binding.
findings.required_fix: Derive the final execution identity inside the transaction from the stored FinalSelection plus typed phase/config/manifests. Include at least selected code, task, environment, and the addendum fields; include protocol as the existing selection contract already binds it.

findings.title: Caller-supplied Snapshot objects are not canonicality-checked
findings.requirement: Snapshot identity must be derived from its immutable bytes rather than accepted as self-attested fields.
findings.evidence: _validate_snapshot_shape checks only four 64-hex fields (558-570); it does not recompute the three file hashes or closure from Snapshot bytes. A Snapshot carrying the real current closure hash but false file hashes and forged bytes was accepted by admit_intent and select_final_method. Selection still copied re-opened current code, so the tested final code was not replaced by the forged bytes.
findings.impact: The public dataclass does not enforce its documented canonical invariant. admit/bind paths treat closure_sha256 as a caller token. This remains conditional on the bridge being trusted, but it weakens auditability and composes badly with historical snapshot storage.
findings.required_fix: Before use, bound byte lengths and recompute every per-file hash and the framed closure from Snapshot bytes, or replace caller-constructible snapshots with private stored snapshot records addressed by a hash that is rederived at storage time.

findings.title: Path and fence guarantees depend on stable trusted roots
findings.requirement: State/source root trust and mount/path assumptions must be explicit; per-file nofollow must not be reported as an OS sandbox.
findings.evidence: A direct source-root symlink was rejected. Exact child names, child symlinks, hardlinks, FIFO, and in-place descriptor mutation were also rejected by code/tests. However, roots are reopened by pathname for each operation (834-838,952-963), ancestor symlinks are followed, and construction does not pin the initial root device/inode. A source-directory replacement was followed; replacing the private state directory permitted a second PENDING admission. There is no no-xdev/mount check. Mount substitution was not attempted because this audit used no privileged operations or Docker.
findings.impact: The T07/T09 guarantees hold for cooperating processes only when trusted source/state roots and their ancestors cannot be renamed, relinked, or remounted. This matches the report's stated TCB and same-UID exclusion, but is not enforced by this module.
findings.required_fix: Either freeze this as an explicit deployment precondition and prove private ownership/permissions/stable absolute roots in root integration, or pin directory FDs/device+inode for the object lifetime and define a deliberate mount policy. Do not claim hostile same-UID/root-swap resistance.

findings.title: The report's T16 test label does not test actual T16
findings.requirement: T16 is extension pre/post byte hash, size, mtime upper bound, loaded absolute source path, prompt/image/argv/tool-census binding; mismatches block R1.
findings.evidence: test_t16_snapshot_hash_is_opened_bytes_not_intent_self_attestation only edits intent.json and compares closure/file hashes (test_trusted_io.py:429-437). trusted-io-report.json associates this with T16, while its limits section separately and correctly says active extension source/loaded-path evidence is outside the module.
findings.impact: The local test is useful but cannot be counted as T16 evidence. The current label can inflate gate coverage despite the disclaimer.
findings.required_fix: Relabel it as a trusted-IO snapshot control with no T16 satisfaction, and leave T16 open until the extension/root lane records the required pre/post/loaded-path receipt.

confirmed_controls.detail: Exact ASCII enum names, NUL/traversal/absolute/confusable rejection, direct final-component nofollow, regular-single-link checks, FIFO rejection, per-file pre-read size cap, in-place mutation detection, and atomic same-directory replacement are supported. Aggregate-cap and root-anchor limits are HPIO-002/006. Unknown-property enforcement belongs to the bridge schema, not this Python API.

The copied 17-test suite reproduced one local PENDING winner across cooperating processes, durable PENDING uncertainty after restart, and stale-lock failure closed. This is local at-most-once admission only; it is not external ORX exactly-once, and state-root substitution is excluded.

Current opened solution bytes are copied to private final-solution.py before state freeze; later tool writes fail FINALIZED, and direct source-path mutation did not change the copied bytes. Arbitrary phase strings fail INVALID_VALUE. Historical candidate selection and real receipt/artifact provenance remain open. Final-run integration must consume the private copy, not reopen mutable source.
No extension load, prompt/image/argv/tool census, pre/post hash, loaded-path, or mtime-upper-bound evidence was produced by these three files.

Then rerun the authored suite plus independent historical-selection, aggregate-cap, identity, root-assumption, and real-receipt integration negatives on the new hashes.
